**What needs to change:** rebuild this leaf against `feature/acp`, so the diff is only the `cancel` ownership/generation check plus its test. The chainlink is being re-labelled so it is not re-dispatched against `main` in the meantime.

This is a dispatch-base defect rather than an executor mistake: chainlink #1215 describes an ACP defect, ACP lives on `feature/acp`, and the worklink base was `main`. The same applies to chainlinks #1221 and #1229, which are also ACP-scoped — I am holding those too.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Retargeted to `feature/acp` and re-reviewed — my earlier request for changes was about the base, and that is resolved.

`feature/acp` was already an ancestor of this branch, so the 78-file / +17,988 diff was purely an artifact of the PR pointing at `main`. Against the correct base it is **10 files, +541/-95**: the cancel fix plus the two already-merged worklink fixes (#1208, #1209) riding along, which `feature/acp` needs from `main` anyway. No rebuild was needed.

On the fix itself:

- It routes through `self._begin_stateful()` rather than inventing a bespoke check, which was an explicit review criterion — `cancel` was the only stateful handler that skipped it, and now it cannot drift from its siblings.
- It checks **both** `state.generation != self._generation` and `state.record.owner_principal != owner`, so a demoted-but-still-connected peer and a foreign principal are both refused.
- The refusal stays a no-op, which is correct for a notification, but is now **observable**: the audit event carries a distinguishable reason (`unauthenticated`, `not_current_connection`, `connection_generation_mismatch`, `session_generation_mismatch`, `session_owner_mismatch`, …). That was the criterion I flagged as easy to skip.

The tests are the part I want to call out. `test_cancel_is_always_a_no_op` is **deleted**, not patched — it only ever cancelled a missing session, so it always hit the `state is None` early-out and asserted a property that was false for any session that existed. The two replacements cancel an **existing** session holding a live `active_prompt` and assert it survives:

- `test_cancel_from_unauthenticated_peer_leaves_existing_session_untouched`
- `test_cancel_from_demoted_connection_leaves_successor_prompt_untouched` — the exact two-editor-window scenario, asserting `running_prompt.done() is False`

That is the criterion the old test failed, and it is now genuinely load-bearing.

CI green (9/9). Merging into `feature/acp`, not `main` — #1463 stays held for 0.9.0.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Confirmed. The current PR scope is still bound to `main`, and this turn's repository tools cannot change a PR's base branch. I did not rebase or push against `main`, since that would preserve the dispatch-base defect.

I've escalated the required operation: change #1481's base to `feature/acp`, then trigger a fresh PR-bound turn so the branch can be reduced and validated as only the `session/cancel` ownership/generation fix plus its test. No repository mutation occurred in this turn.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1213: web_ui: turns cursor paging is unbounded, so an absent ?after= cursor materializes the whole turns.jsonl

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving. The fix went to the right layer.

- The bound is pushed **into `tail_jsonl_records`** as an optional `max_records`, so future callers inherit it rather than each re-deriving a cap. That was the design question I raised in the review criteria and this is the better answer.
- **All three helpers** are covered — `_turns_after_page`, `_turns_before_page`, `_turns_tail_page` each pass `_TURNS_MAX_SCAN_RECORDS` — so the two sibling vectors close with the primary one. Fixing only `?after=` would have left `?limit=99999999` and `?before=<unknown>` open.
- `limit` is clamped to `_TURNS_MAX_PAGE_RECORDS` at the query-parsing sites.
- An absent cursor is now **distinguishable from an empty page** — a `cursor_not_found` code carrying `scan_limit` — so a client cannot mistake a truncated scan for end-of-data. That was an explicit criterion and it would have been easy to skip.
- `test_turn_cursor_helpers_bound_decoded_records` asserts on records **decoded**, not merely returned. Capping the response while still parsing the whole file would have left the pathology intact and passed a careless reading of the criteria.

This is a regression of a documented fix — `_read_jsonl`'s 5000-record cap exists for exactly this — so having the bound live in the shared tail reader is the outcome that prevents a third occurrence.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1210: secret_scan: commit/push refusal gate misses credential shapes the redactor already recognises

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving. Every acceptance criterion is met, including the two most likely to be skipped.

- All six shapes land: `ghs_`/`ghu_`/`ghr_`, Discord bot token, `xoxa`, and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=`.
- **Both copies are aligned** — `mimir/secret_scan.py` and the BRE in `mimir/templates/git/pre-commit`, with `test_pre_commit_template_matches_credential_corpus` proving it. A fix touching only the Python side would have left scaffolded deployments weaker than the factory path.
- `test_refusal_gate_is_not_weaker_than_redactor_for_credential_corpus` enforces the drift invariant directly against `redact_text`, so the gate cannot silently fall behind the redactor again. That was the criterion I cared most about, since the drift is what produced the defect.
- False positives are bounded by a named benign corpus, and it includes the adversarial case — `def verify_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_assignment(value)` — where the key NAME appears without a secret. A gate that refuses ordinary code gets worked around, so this matters.

Note this closes the second of two independent bypasses of the publication gate; the binary-blob bypass landed in #1476, so that gate is now sound on both axes.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1212: tools: model-supplied mimir_direct_argv survives on non-shell tools and hijacks the next nested shell_exec

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving. This fixes the invariant rather than the instance.

The strip is now **unconditional** — the tool-name gate moved below it, so `_SERVER_ONLY_SHELL_ARGS` are removed from every tool and only the trusted-service argv *replacement* stays gated. That is the right split: the leaf's invariant is "server-only keys are never model-supplied, for any tool", and an extended allowlist would have re-created the same drift.

The bind sites now gate on tool name independently (sync `:1500`, async `:1784`), so the two sites cannot diverge again even if one is edited later.

The tests satisfy the criterion I was most concerned about — they assert on the argv that would **actually execute**, not merely that the outer request was cleaned:

- `executed == [["bash", "-lc", login_shell_command("git status --short")]]` — the nested `shell_exec` runs its own command, not the planted one
- the same for `bash_async` via `spawned`
- `test_non_shell_execution_never_binds_direct_argv` asserts `observed == [None, None]` across both sync and async `task` calls
- `mimir_shell_refusal` is checked too, so the whole server-only set is covered rather than just `mimir_direct_argv`

Load-bearing: without the change `executed` would be `[["/bin/sh", "-c", "planted"]]`, so the test fails on revert.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1211: cred_rotate: not_implemented probes make every Type B/C rotation roll back to the revoked secret

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving.

The fix makes "unverifiable" a genuine third outcome rather than special-casing a message: `ProbeStatus` is `passed|failed|skipped`, and the rotation branches on `probe.kind == "not_implemented"`. My review criterion explicitly required deciding on the probe KIND rather than string-matching the detail text, and that is what landed.

Checked against the leaf:

- **Skip completes the rotation** — `_execute` takes the skip branch, no rollback, exit 0, and `compose.env` retains the new value.
- **The operator is not told it was verified** — `verify_summary` reads "verification skipped (no probe implemented for …)", `render()` prints `SKIP`, and `run_verify_creds_cmd` reports "N skipped" separately from failures.
- **Genuine failures still roll back** — the existing failure test now also asserts `stage == "verify"` and `rolled_back is True`, so the fix cannot degenerate into "never roll back".
- **The fixture gap is closed.** This was the specific thing I asked for: `fake_registry` no longer monkeypatches `_PACKAGE_MANIFEST` away, so `test_rotate_skips_unimplemented_probe_from_shipped_registry` drives the REAL shipped `DISCORD_TOKEN` entry rather than a fabricated one. That wholesale replacement is why every prior rotation test was blind to the shipped probe kinds.

CI: `pytest (3.11)` failed on first run inside `test_built_image_provides_process_tools` — a Docker build fetching s6-overlay, `curl` exit 22 — while 3.12 passed the same suite. That is a network flake unrelated to this change; I re-ran the job and it is green. Not treating it as pre-existing breakage, and not waiving it.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1209: worklink: staged-secret gate scans only diff + lines, so any file git treats as binary bypasses it

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving.

The fix takes the structural route rather than the cheap one: it reads staged **blobs** via `git cat-file blob :<path>` instead of trusting `git diff`'s rendering. That closes both bypasses at once rather than patching the symptom — adding `--text` would have handled the NUL byte and left the `.gitattributes -diff` case open.

Checked against the leaf's criteria:

- **Both bypasses covered by test** — `test_commit_checkout_changes_refuses_secret_in_staged_blob` is parametrized over a NUL-byte blob and a `.gitattributes` `-diff` marking, so the executor cannot control scannability.
- **Unscannable means refuse**, and it is explicit rather than incidental: both the path-listing failure and the blob-read failure raise, and the non-bytes cases raise too. `test_commit_checkout_changes_names_unreadable_staged_path` and `..._with_invalid_blob_output` pin it.
- **Legitimate binary still commits** — `test_commit_checkout_changes_commits_clean_binary_blob` uses a PNG signature with invalid UTF-8, so the gate did not become a blanket refusal of binary content.
- **`surrogateescape`** is the right decode choice: every byte survives and ASCII secret shapes are unchanged, so binary is scanned rather than skipped.
- **The secret is still not echoed**; the error names only the path, which is a genuine improvement for diagnosis.
- `text=False` is threaded through every runner variant, and `ControllerGitPublication.run` already accepted `text`, so the publication path is covered too.

The guard is load-bearing: under the old `+`-line scan a NUL-bearing blob renders as "Binary files differ", so the new test fails if the change is reverted.

Note this closes one of two independent bypasses of the same gate — the pattern-set gap is chainlink #1210 and is still open, so the gate is not yet fully sound.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1208: authz: every service shell profile admits an unconstrained jq filter, so jq env reads the whole process environment

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approving.

Verified the fix does what the leaf required rather than the easy thing:

- **Environment scrub, not a filter denylist.** `direct_exec_env` gives a jq argv only `PATH`/`HOME`/`LANG`/`TZ`/`LC_*`, so the guarantee holds regardless of how the filter is written. The code comment says so explicitly, which is the right place for it.
- **Not scoped to `--null-input`.** Tests cover `jq env sample.json`, `jq '$ENV.GITHUB_TOKEN' sample.json` and `jq -r '$ENV|tostring' sample.json` — the forms that would have survived an option-level fix.
- **All four profiles**, and both `direct_exec_env` and `direct_exec_env_overlay`.
- **The property is not skip-only.** `test_real_jq_cannot_read_parent_credentials_and_still_filters_json` skips without a jq binary, but `test_jq_direct_exec_env_contains_only_non_secret_process_settings` asserts on the env dict unconditionally, and the access-control test asserts `sentinel not in direct_exec_env(argv)`. Both fail if the `_is_jq_argv` branch is removed, so the guard is load-bearing.
- **Legitimate jq preserved** — `jq -r .name sample.json` still parses and still produces correct output.

Also credit for the additional finding in the PR body: `cat`/`head`/`tail` on `/proc/self/environ` reach the same disclosure. I reproduced it in the container against the real environment — it leaks GITHUB_TOKEN, DISCORD_TOKEN, MIMIR_API_KEY and VOYAGE_API_KEY under the `maintenance` profile — and filed it as chainlink #1243 rather than expanding this leaf. Scoping it out here was the right call.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(acp): wire reply delivery and correct ACP channel labelling (preparatory)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
The delivery-mode diagnosis is correct, and suppressing the impossible `interactive_turn_no_send_message` warning specifically under `acp_delivery` is well scoped. The new positive/empty-output tests cover the basic behavior, and all nine GitHub checks are green.

I found two blocking correctness issues in the ACP publication path:

1. The reply is sourced from `TurnRecord.output`, which is deliberately capped at 2,048 characters for persistence/telemetry. That makes ACP delivery silently truncate otherwise valid long answers. Delivery needs an untruncated output value separate from the bounded record field, with a >2,048-character regression test.
2. `queue.join()` drains only the bus-forwarding queue. `_forward_updates` submits into `UpdateDispatcher`'s second queue and then marks the first item done, so the final answer can race ahead of pending tool updates. Drain the dispatcher before publishing the `agent_message_chunk`, and make the ordering test deterministic enough to expose the two-queue race.

I posted both findings inline. Local focused execution could not start because the bound test runner rejected traversal of its generated checkout (`test_path_permission_denied` on a mode-0700 `.venv`/checkout ancestor), so my test evidence is the green CI matrix rather than an additional local run.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
The remediation correctly resolves both prior findings at the mechanism level: delivery now uses the untruncated harness output, and routing through `ACPBridge` / `_OrderedTurnPublisher` preserves update ordering. The ACP-specific substantiveness bypass is narrowly gated, the off-ACP behavior remains pinned, and the added long-output regression proves delivery differs from the intentionally capped `TurnRecord.output`.

One blocking end-to-end issue remains. The prompt event runs on `acp:<session-id>` but carries the connection-scoped auth context created for `acp:stdio`; the explicit-session-binding path preserves that mismatched triggering channel. Consequently IFC still refuses `harness_auto_deliver` with `ifc_label_blocked:same_channel`, as the remediation note confirms. The current unit tests monkeypatch `acp_delivery=True` and use a generic event, so they bypass this actual ACP authorization boundary and cannot establish the PR title's promised behavior. Please either include the safe per-session auth-context scoping fix here, or explicitly rescope this as a preparatory slice with the functional dependent change, and add a boundary test that authenticates, prompts on a real ACP session, and observes the final `agent_message_chunk`.

Validation: both Python matrix jobs and the other visible checks pass, but `pytest-enforced` is currently failing. I therefore cannot approve this head even apart from the functional blocker.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
The per-session auth-context narrowing is sound: it changes only `channel_id`/`resource_id`, retains the connection's authority fields, and the new test pins that behavior. The previously failing enforced suite is also green at this head, along with the full visible CI matrix.

The advertised ACP delivery path is still not functional end to end, however. The remediation comment confirms that real ACP turns continue to refuse `harness_auto_deliver` because preloaded `protected_prompt` sources fail the all-sources SAME_CHANNEL check. Correspondingly, `test_prompt_auth_context_is_scoped_to_the_session_channel` proves only the intermediate context rewrite; it does not satisfy the prior request for a boundary test that authenticates, prompts through a real ACP session, and observes the final `agent_message_chunk`.

That remaining trust-derivation question may reasonably require a separate operator-policy change, but then this PR must be explicitly scoped and titled as preparatory infrastructure rather than as delivering the turn output, with the functional dependency tracked. As currently titled/scoped, it still claims behavior that the author has measured as refused live, so I cannot approve it.

Validation: all nine current-head GitHub checks are green, including `pytest-enforced` and Python 3.11/3.12. I did not run an additional local suite; the blocker is the acknowledged live authorization failure and missing end-to-end assertion, not a speculative test failure.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
The revised scope resolves my remaining objection. The title and PR body now state plainly that this is preparatory infrastructure, not an end-to-end ACP delivery fix, and they track the remaining `protected_prompt` trust-derivation blocker as #1260 rather than implying it is solved here.

Within that narrower scope, the implementation is sound: ACP final text enters the existing ordered channel-delivery path with the untruncated harness output; ACP alone bypasses the recovery opt-in and substantiveness floor; the impossible resend nudge is skipped; prompt/authentication events share a bridge instance; and the connection auth context is narrowed to the server-generated session channel without changing principal or roles. The tests pin the ACP/off-ACP behavior, long-answer delivery, missed-reply bookkeeping, and per-session auth-context rewrite.

The absent end-to-end `agent_message_chunk` assertion is now an explicit dependency of #1260, where that test can exercise the real enforced boundary instead of stubbing away the current refusal. All nine current-head checks are green, including `pytest-enforced` and Python 3.11/3.12. I found no further blocking issue in this preparatory slice.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
## Remediation pushed (`ed4ea07e`) — both review findings addressed

Rather than patch the two defects in place, I moved delivery onto the existing
harness path, `_maybe_auto_deliver_final_text`, which resolves both at their root:

**1. Truncation.** Confirmed: `mimir/agent.py:3109` does `output=(output or "")[:2048]`.
Delivery is now fed the harness's untruncated turn output rather than
`TurnRecord.output`, so the cap stays correct for persistence and no longer
governs the wire. Pinned by a >2,048-character regression test that also asserts
`len(record.output) == 2048`, so it cannot pass by both values being untruncated.

**2. Ordering.** Confirmed: `dispatcher.submit()` only calls `self.enqueue(event)`,
so `queue.join()` returning means submitted, not published. Rather than
hand-sequencing drains, delivery goes through the channel registry to the
ACPBridge's bound `_OrderedTurnPublisher`, which already does
`queue.join()` -> `dispatcher.drain()` -> publish. That is the primitive the
codebase already had for this; my first version bypassed it.

### Two further defects this surfaced

* **The substantiveness floor would have eaten most ACP replies.**
  `_substantive_final_text` requires >= 20 chars and >= 3 words — a sound bar for
  optional recovery, fatal when it is the only delivery path. Every live answer I
  tested ("Paris", "Jupiter", "Blue") is below it. Bypassed for ACP only, with a
  test, plus a companion test that the floor still applies off ACP.
* **`bridge_instance` drift.** The prompt event omitted it, so `access_control`
  fell back to `event.source` ("acp") while the authenticate event was labelled
  "acp-stdio". Both now share one constant. Measured before/after: that field
  agrees.

Full suite: **9604 passed, 27 skipped**. The first remediation attempt broke 7
tests (`test_resend_nudge`, `test_information_flow`) because the nudge path binds
`self` to a `SimpleNamespace` stub; `_is_acp_delivery_turn` is module-level for
that reason.

## Not yet working end to end — one blocker remains

This PR is necessary but **not sufficient**. Live, the reply is still refused:

```
sink_blocked  sink=harness_auto_deliver  reason=ifc_label_blocked:same_channel
```

Instrumenting `_source_is_triggering_channel_compatible` in the container gives
the exact comparison:

```
princ  'jason'           vs 'jason'            match
dom    'channel:private' vs 'channel:private'  match
bi     'acp-stdio'       vs 'acp-stdio'        match   <- fixed here
chan   'acp:3dbfdbe6...' vs 'acp:stdio'        MISMATCH
```

The sources are labelled with the **session** channel, but
`resolved_triggering` comes from `auth_context.channel_id`, and the ACP auth
context is built once per **connection** at authenticate against `acp:stdio`
(`_auth_context_for` returns `connection.auth_context`). Every prompt turn runs
on `acp:<session-id>`, so a reply to the turn's own channel can never satisfy
the same-channel check.

I have deliberately **not** fixed that here. The correction is to re-scope an
`AuthContext` — a `frozen=True` carrier whose docstring says it is frozen
"to prevent post-creation widening" — on a surface that forces
`enforcement_enabled=True` regardless of `MIMIR_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENFORCED`. That
belongs in its own reviewed change, not folded into a delivery fix.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
## Second remediation (`9cf0a65a`)

Both blocking points from the last review are addressed, plus the failing check.

### `pytest-enforced`

Fixed, and the cause was my test setup rather than the code. The four ACP tests
assert delivery *happens*; under enforcement the sink gate needs a principal to
establish channel compatibility, and I had omitted `author`/`source` on the
events. The existing passing auto-deliver test sets both — mine now match it.

Worth recording: my scripted patch reported "5/5 patched" while matching the
wrong occurrences, leaving three tests unfixed. Only a per-function audit caught
it. Both suites now run clean: **9605 passed, 27 skipped, with and without
`MIMIR_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENFORCED=1`**.

### Per-session auth-context scoping

Included here, as suggested. `_auth_context_for` now narrows the connection's
context to the session's channel.

Kept deliberately minimal — only `channel_id` and `resource_id` change;
`principal`, `canonical_principal`, `roles`, `is_service` and
`enforcement_enabled` carry through untouched. It narrows rather than widens:
the caller already verifies the connection principal owns the session, and
`thread_id` is server-generated (`acp:{uuid4}`) and revalidated on load
(`session_store._validate_payload`), so a client cannot steer the context at
another channel.

`test_prompt_auth_context_is_scoped_to_the_session_channel` authenticates,
prompts on a real ACP session, and asserts both the narrowing and that every
authority field is preserved. It fails when the scoping is reverted.

### Measured effect

Instrumenting `_source_is_triggering_channel_compatible` in the container, the
channel source now matches on every field — `b` and `c` previously did not:

```
p 'jason'/'jason'   d 'channel:private'/'channel:private'
b 'acp-stdio'/'acp-stdio'   c 'acp:3e608bd2…'/'acp:3e608bd2…'
```

### Still not end-to-end — and now precisely bounded

Delivery is still refused live, but for a different and final reason. Two
further sources are present on an ACP turn:

```
DBG complete=True kind='protected_prompt' authz=frozenset({'jason'}) eff='jason'
DBG complete=True kind='protected_prompt' authz=frozenset({'jason'}) eff='jason'
```

That branch passes only when `source.integrity == "trusted"` or the source's
resource belongs to this channel. These preloaded prompt blocks are neither, and
the SAME_CHANNEL check is all-or-nothing, so one non-conforming source refuses
the whole flow.

That is the self-authored-context trust-derivation work — labelling the agent's
own preloaded prompt/memory context as trusted rather than untrusted ingest —
not an ACP defect. Changing what counts as trusted input is an operator policy
decision and does not belong in a delivery fix. Flagging it as the single
remaining dependency rather than folding it in.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Independent review (cannot formally approve — authored by this account; mimir-carreira's APPROVED is on the current head `33e71b7a1`). CI green 9/9, base `feature/acp`.

**Reads correct to me.** The scoping is the strongest part: the body states plainly that this does *not* make ACP replies work end to end, names the remaining blocker as chainlink #1260, and records that it was retitled because the earlier framing "claimed behavior I had measured as refused live, which was wrong to advertise." A PR that narrows its own claim after measuring is worth more than one that quietly overstates.

**The labelling fix is at the root.** Hoisting `_ACP_BRIDGE_INSTANCE = "acp-stdio"` into one constant used by *both* the `acp_authenticate` and `user_message` events fixes the real asymmetry: the authenticate event carried `bridge_instance`, the prompt event omitted it and fell back to `event.source` ("acp"), so `_source_is_triggering_channel_compatible` compared "acp-stdio" against "acp" and refused every reply to the originating channel. Two literals that had to agree is exactly the shape that drifts.

**Every behaviour change is paired with its negative case**, which is what I check hardest:
- `test_acp_turn_auto_delivers_final_text_without_opt_in` / `test_non_acp_turn_keeps_the_auto_deliver_opt_in`
- `test_acp_delivers_replies_below_the_substantiveness_floor` / `test_non_acp_turn_keeps_the_substantiveness_floor`
- plus `test_acp_delivery_is_not_truncated_at_the_turn_record_cap` and `test_acp_turn_logs_no_forgot_to_send_signal`

so the ACP carve-out cannot silently widen to ordinary turns.

**One item I had filed against this area is now obsolete.** Chainlink #1239 originally carried an ACP double-delivery item — the unconditional `agent_message_chunk` publish in `_run_prompt` racing `_maybe_auto_deliver_final_text`. This work removes that publish and routes delivery through the single gated path, so I edited that item out of #1239 rather than leave an executor chasing a fixed defect.

Leaving the merge decision to you, since #1260 is an operator-policy call and this is the ACP branch.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1207: saga: reasoning_effort is hardcoded to none on the codex_plus path, so the saga.toml setting is silently dropped

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approved. Verified against the leaf's acceptance and review criteria, not just read.

**Design — took the right direction.** The shared table went into a new
`mimir/_reasoning_effort.py` rather than importing `mimir.agent` into
`mimir/saga/_llm.py`. That was the leaf's main review criterion: saga is
self-contained, and reaching into agent.py would have pulled langchain and
deepagents in for a lookup table.

**The trap is genuinely guarded.** The call passes the *hyphenated*
`"codex-plus"`, so validation actually runs. This was the criterion a naive
implementation would have silently failed — `_EFFORT_LEVELS` is keyed by
hyphenated name and returns unknown providers unchanged, so passing saga's
underscored `codex_plus` would have accepted any garbage while passing every
other test.

**Mutation-tested both directions** (worktree at ccff9b26):

- reverting `reasoning_effort=reasoning_effort` -> `"none"` fails
  `test_codex_plus_resolves_reasoning_effort_precedence[llm-fallback]` and
  `[subsystem-override]`
- flipping `"codex-plus"` -> `"codex_plus"` fails
  `test_codex_plus_rejects_invalid_resolved_reasoning_effort`

Both tests execute; nothing skipped or deselected (11 passed in the file).

**Default is preserved** — the built-in-default case pins `"none"`, so the
cheap-inference floor is not silently raised for existing deployments. That was
the one way this change could have cost real money everywhere.

**Checked the raised-outside-`try` question.** `validate_effort` runs before the
`try`, so a bad config value propagates rather than returning `""` as the module
docstring promises. Not a defect: all three saga call sites
(`query_rewrite.py:169`, `synthesize.py:480`, `:530`) wrap `call_llm` in
`except Exception`, so it degrades as designed.

**Scope respected** — only the codex_plus path threads an effort;
anthropic / openai_compat / claude_code still send none, as required.

Full suite green: 9018 passed, 27 skipped.

One deliberate non-blocker for the record: the moved validator's message no
longer names `MIMIR_MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`. That is correct now that it serves
both the env var and saga.toml — naming one surface would mislead users of the
other, and the message still carries the invalid value, the provider, and the
valid set.

Not merging — that is the operator's call.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: release: 0.8.4

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Verdict: APPROVE

This is a clean patch-release cut: `pyproject.toml` and the editable package entry in `uv.lock` are both advanced from 0.8.3 to 0.8.4, with no dependency or Dockerfile changes. The changelog entry is scoped consistently with the release diff and clearly distinguishes operator-visible fixes, new authority mechanisms, and internal test portability work.

Validation is appropriate for this metadata-only release PR: all nine reported checks pass, including Python 3.11/3.12 pytest, enforced-access-control pytest, package build, frontend, skill conformance, Claude Code smoke, Chainlink audit, and Worklink image identity. No blocking findings.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: 1467 : authz: operator can vouch for a turn's ingested sources once per sink category, pinned to the label state (supersedes #1059)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
The receipt-based binding and post-approval source invalidation are careful, and the test matrix covers many race/fail-closed cases. I found two blocking issues:

1. The reusable category capability is consumable only when `_current_turn` is present, regressing the durable `AuthContext` IFC contract for SDK/MCP/task forks that retain the authentic carrier but lose the ContextVar. I left an inline comment on `access_control.py` with the required carrier-based fix and regression test.
2. The operator-facing consent prompt directly interpolates untrusted provenance fields and does not disclose that this is a category-wide, any-tool/any-destination grant for the remainder of the turn. Newline/control characters can spoof the rendered approval text. I left an inline comment on `registry.py` requesting unambiguous escaping, explicit scope disclosure, and adversarial rendering tests.

I also recommend, non-blocking for this revision, moving the newly expanded injected-message IFC fold/category-install work behind a fail-closed exception boundary so a malformed source/resolver failure cannot abort the model boundary after the queue was drained, and adding table-driven real-tool coverage across every eligible sink category (especially spawn, scheduler, proposal, and forge) to prove category approval bypasses only IFC compatibility—not independent RBAC/scope/argument gates.

Validation: reviewed the full 2,675-line bounded diff at head `4d46993fc0d27d5ac426ed7cfdbf452dc8b26fe7`; all reported CI checks are green. I did not rerun the suite locally because CI completed successfully on this exact head.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Re-reviewed at `2c494d37ca9b2c3d3fd0d2c3aae98cc28bfbade8`. Both prior blockers are resolved:

- Reusable category authority is now bound once to the durable `InformationFlowState` carried by `AuthContext`; contextless genuine-carrier execution remains admitted, while present-context state/turn mismatches and different-state carriers fail closed. The new regression exercises the lost-`_current_turn` path and repeated use.
- Every dynamic approval-prompt field is JSON-rendered with ASCII escaping, and the prompt explicitly states that approval covers every tool and destination in the category for the rest of the turn while labeling tool/target as non-binding context. The adversarial test pins the complete alert and proves raw C0 controls other than structural LF are absent.

The source-fold receipt and live-label equality checks still invalidate category authority on later source arrival, and category eligibility remains explicitly exhaustive. All current CI checks, including Python 3.11/3.12 and enforced pytest, are green. Approved.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Merging on mimir's approval at `2c494d37c`. Independently verified the property the design rests on before merging.

**The grant dies on new ingest — confirmed, and it is enforced twice.**

Single-line mutations all survived, which initially looked like a coverage gap. It is not: there are two independent mechanisms and either alone is sufficient.

- `InformationFlowState` clears `_sink_category_capabilities` outright when a source arrives or labels change (`models.py:394-395`)
- consumption independently re-checks `capability.labels == live.labels == current.labels`, and the same for `source_channels` and `sources` (`models.py:526-528`)

Removing either leaves the suite green because the other holds. Removing **both** fails four tests by name:

```
test_later_tool_source_class_invalidates_authenticated_category_capability[fetch]
test_later_tool_source_class_invalidates_authenticated_category_capability[search]
test_later_tool_source_class_invalidates_authenticated_category_capability[file-read]
test_later_ingested_message_invalidates_authenticated_category_capability
```

So ingested content cannot introduce fresh instructions after the operator approves and then ride the grant, which is the whole security argument for scoping to a category rather than an action.

Full suite on macOS: **9007 passed, 17 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

Also recording that mimir's two blockers on `4d46993fc` were substantive and correctly fixed: binding reusable authority to the durable `InformationFlowState` carrier rather than a ContextVar (so SDK/MCP/task forks keep the authentic carrier), and JSON-escaping every dynamic field in the approval prompt with explicit scope disclosure — an approval prompt that can be spoofed by control characters in untrusted provenance is worse than no prompt.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1206: worklink: the execution copy is chowned but never chmodded, so the runner is locked out of the directory made for it

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `d4a4d0cd4`. The fix itself is right — this is the approach I hoped for. One blocking item: the new test cannot run on macOS, which re-breaks the cross-platform suite that #1469 fixed a few hours ago.

## Blocking — `test_uv_execution_copy_normalizes_for_runner_without_relaxing_source` fails on macOS

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: /proc/self/fd/11
  shutil.copytree(f"/proc/self/fd/{checkout_fd}", project, symlinks=True)
```

It exercises `_execution_checkout_fd`, which copies from `/proc/self/fd/<n>`. macOS has no procfs, so the test errors before reaching any assertion. It fails on unmodified `main` too once this lands — I confirmed the other 19 tests in the file pass there, so this is the only one.

That matters because it is the same class #1469 just removed. `main` is currently green on macOS (8904 passed, 0 failed) for the first time this session, and #1194 tracks keeping it that way.

The production path is legitimately Linux-only — `worker_exec.py` touches `/proc` at :85, :117, :184, :223, :308, and the containment worker only runs in the container. So the honest fix is to say so, not to contort the test. **The repository already has the precedent**, used twice in `tests/test_worklink_cli.py`:

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(not Path("/proc").is_dir(), reason="requires procfs")
```

Please mark it the same way. A skip that states the reason is accurate; a failure that says nothing is not.

## Confirmed — the fix is the right one

- **It reuses `_normalize_checkout_fd` instead of duplicating mode logic a third time.** That was the review criterion I cared most about: #1200 fixed the execute bits, #1201 fixed the `uv.toml` EACCES, and a third hand-rolled copy of the mode rules would have guaranteed a fourth variant. Sharing the routine means the two paths cannot drift again.
- **`_prepare_boundary` is untouched.** Confirmed by diff: no change to `mimir/contained_checkout.py`. The `0700` source boundary is the isolation property and it survives.
- **The normalization is correct for the consumer** — `_normalize_checkout_fd` sets the root `0o2770` owned `MIMIR_UID:WORKLINK_GID`, so the runner at uid 1002 gets group `rwx` on the copy it is meant to use.
- **The test asserts the right things**, once it can run: nested directories traversable, files `0o660`, executables `0o770`, no world bits, the symlink preserved without following it (the external target stays `0o600`), the copy removed afterwards, and — the important one — `stat.S_IMODE(source.stat().st_mode) == 0o700` with the source still inaccessible to the runner. That last pair is what rejects the wrong fix.
- **Failure is no longer silently skipped.** Dropping the `if os.geteuid() == 0` guard means a normalization failure raises instead of leaving an unusable copy. Correct for a root worker, and the `except: os.close(project_fd); raise` avoids leaking the fd.

I could not run the mutations meaningfully because the test errors at baseline on this host. Once the skip marker lands I will re-run them and, if the guards hold, approve.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Re-reviewed at `352daa772`. The blocking item is resolved with exactly the repository's existing precedent:

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(not Path("/proc").is_dir(), reason="requires procfs")
```

macOS now reports it alongside two sibling skips that already state their platform requirement, so the reason is visible rather than silent:

```
SKIPPED tests/test_worklink_worker_exec.py:194  requires procfs
SKIPPED tests/test_worklink_worker_exec.py:458  requires Linux root to exercise the executor identity boundary
SKIPPED tests/test_worklink_worker_exec.py:572  the shipped-image proof exercises this real uid boundary in CI
```

Full suite on macOS: **8931 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`, where the test actually executes rather than skipping — so the guard is exercised on the platform that has procfs.

## Verified the mechanism directly, since the test skips on this host

A skip means I cannot mutate the guard locally, so I measured the property against the real `_normalize_checkout_fd` on Linux as root — the production identity — with the runner attempting access as uid 1002:

```
WITHOUT normalization: copy mode=700   runner_can_access=False   <- the defect
WITH    normalization: copy mode=2770  runner_can_access=True    <- the fix
source boundary after: mode=700   runner_can_access=False        <- isolation intact
```

That is the whole leaf in three lines: the copy becomes usable by the identity it was made for, and the `0700` source boundary is untouched.

One note on my own method: my first run of that probe reported `runner_can_access=False` even after normalization, which looked like the fix failing. It was my harness — `tempfile.mkdtemp` creates the parent at `0700` owned by root, so traversal was blocked before reaching the copy at all. Corrected the parent mode and the property held. Recording it because a wrong "the fix does not work" claim would have been worse than no measurement.

Everything from the prior review still stands: `_normalize_checkout_fd` is reused rather than duplicating mode logic a third time, `_prepare_boundary` is untouched, the test asserts nested traversal, `0o660` files, `0o770` executables, no world bits, the symlink preserved without following it, cleanup, and the source staying inaccessible.

Approved.

payload.body:

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
No code-level blockers found in the diff. The replacement test is materially better isolated: its fake `uv` gives a real negative control, directly observes the environment passed by `RepoProjectTests`, preserves the fd-entered checkout path, and avoids coupling the assertion to the installed uv version, `/proc`, or root's permission semantics. The declaration change is also pinned both by exact-key validation and by the 30-minute value assertion.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Re-reviewed at `c4c95daddd43da019dea7d17000fd4eefce5159d`: **APPROVE**.

The condition from my prior comment is now satisfied: all nine checks are complete and green, including pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.12 plus `pytest-enforced`. The platform-independent fake-`uv` regression directly pins `UV_NO_CONFIG=1` with a meaningful negative control while preserving the fd-entered checkout behavior, and the factory declaration both admits and fixes the verify timeout at 30 minutes.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
The condition you withheld on is satisfied — all three pytest jobs finished green at `c4c95dad`:

```
package=SUCCESS  skill-conformance=SUCCESS  worklink-image-identity=SUCCESS
claude-code-extra-smoke=SUCCESS  frontend=SUCCESS  chainlink-cli-audit=SUCCESS
pytest (3.11)=SUCCESS  pytest (3.12)=SUCCESS  pytest-enforced=SUCCESS
```

9/9. Re-requesting review so the comment can become a verdict.

On the runner refusal you hit: that is a real defect and it is not this PR. `_execution_checkout_fd` (`mimir/worklink/worker_exec.py`) copies the checkout and chowns to `MIMIR_UID`/`WORKLINK_GID` but never chmods, so source modes survive the copy. The two containment paths disagree on this:

| path | modes |
|---|---|
| `_normalize_directory_fd` | dirs `0o2770`, files `0o660\|exec` — group-accessible |
| `_execution_checkout_fd` | copy + chown only — source modes preserved |

Same family as #1200 (execute bits lost in the normalization path) and #1201 (the `uv.toml` EACCES), but in the copy path, which has no normalization at all. payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1205: poller: a refused remediation turn is charged as a successful attempt, so a blocked PR burns its whole retry budget and reports gave_up

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `1a8d7c129`. The diagnosis is sharper than the leaf I wrote, and every guard is pinned.

## The leaf had the wrong location; this found the right one

I scoped this to the poller script. The real defect was upstream: `attempt_disposition` in `mimir/agent.py` ALREADY exempted hard refusals —

```python
"attempt_disposition": "exempt_hard_refusal" if hard_refusals else "charge"
```

— but the refusals in question were never recorded as `hard_boundary_denials` in the first place, so a blocked turn looked like a clean one. `_record_tool_outcome` in `budget_gate.py` now wires the paths that were silently dropping them: `ToolPolicyRefusal`, `service_shell_refusal`, the standing-review denial, the integrity-metadata write refusal, and `unsupported_operation` — on both the sync and async handlers.

Fixing it at the poller would have papered over a framework-level gap that affects every consumer of `attempt_disposition`, not just the changes-requested cursor. Good call.

## The partial-turn guard

`remediation_effects` on `TurnContext` records server-observed successes for `repo_commit`, `repo_push`, `pr_comment`, `pr_inline_review_comment`, `pr_rerequest_review`, and the disposition becomes

```python
refusal_is_exempt = bool(hard_refusals and not remediation_effects)
```

so a turn that pushed a fix and was refused later is still charged. That closes the loophole a naive "exempt on refusal" fix would have opened.

## Mutations

- drop the `remediation_effects` guard → fails `test_framework_charges_refusal_after_remediation_effect`
- stop recording `ToolPolicyRefusal` → fails `test_tool_refusal_is_a_result_and_next_tool_call_can_run`
- stop treating `unsupported_operation` as a refusal → fails the same test
- **exempt content failures too** (`refusal_is_exempt = not remediation_effects`, the over-correction I was most worried about) → fails `test_run_turn_emits_turn_failed_event_on_error`

That last one matters: the risk in this change was an unfixable PR retrying forever because every failure reads as a refusal. It is pinned.

## Confirmed against the leaf

- Classification is server-derived — `hard_boundary_denials` and `remediation_effects` are framework-authored from boundary middleware state. The in-code comment says so and the call sites bear it out; a turn cannot self-report a refusal to earn a free retry.
- Content failures, model/framework failures, test failures, and normal completions with no external effect all stay charged.
- Exempt refusals keep their named reason (`poller_recovery.py` now sets `attempt_reasons` from `outcome_reason`), surface immediately through the durable refusal event, and still wait for the existing 24-hour backstop — so a blocked PR does not go silent, and the exemption is bounded rather than an unbounded retry.

## Suite

Full suite locally: **8914 passed, 16 skipped, 1 failed**. The failure is `test_uv_config_search_is_bounded_at_unsearchable_snapshot_boundary`, which is environmental on my machine — my `uv` lives under `$HOME` so the scrubber flags it as a controller path and the test never reaches its assertion. It is unrelated to this PR and fails identically on `main`. CI is 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`, and the PR reports the enforced gate at 8,920 passed.

Approved. Not merging.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1203: authz: no server-authenticated operator approval exists — record the grant from the operator's own injected message, not from a model tool call (blocks #1198)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `e4ac172dc`. The design is right and the hard parts are handled well. One blocking gap: the single guard the whole leaf rests on is not pinned by any test.

## Blocking — the admin/non-service check on the responder survives deletion

`_is_authenticated_operator` ends with:

```python
return access.is_admin and not access.is_service and resolver.resolve(event.author) is not None
```

Replace it with `return resolver.resolve(event.author) is not None` and `tests/test_mid_turn_injection.py` is **40 passed**. Nothing fails.

That check is the leaf. Without it, any identity the resolver can resolve records a grant — including a NON-ADMIN user posting in the operator alert channel. The fixture already makes this reachable: `_resolver` defines `operator` (`slack-U1`, `roles: [admin]`) and `user` (`slack-U2`, `roles: [user]`), but no test ever sends `slack-U2` through `record_authenticated_response`. The `is_service=True` at line 479 is on the *requesting* AuthContext for the autonomous-trigger test, not the responder.

This is the criterion the leaf named — every refusal pinned by a test that fails when the refusal is deleted — applied to the one refusal that defines the primitive. Please add the non-admin responder case (and a service-identity responder) asserting `unauthenticated_operator`. `slack-U2` is already in the fixture, so it is a few lines.

The other two mutations are properly pinned, which is what makes this one stand out:

- allow autonomous/service turns to request → fails `test_autonomous_turns_cannot_create_approval_request` for all three of `scheduled_tick`, `saga_session_end`, `upgrade`
- accept any reply text as approval → fails `test_nonmatching_declined_timed_out_and_unreachable_requests_fail_closed`

## Confirmed — the design holds

I went looking for a way for the model to manufacture a grant and did not find one.

- **Identity and ingress are server-owned.** The reply text only selects approve/decline; `trigger == "user_message"`, a real `author`, a non-empty `source` outside `{api, stdin, web}`, and the absence of the HTTP-ingress marker all come from the `AgentEvent`, and the principal comes from `IdentityResolver`. The model cannot synthesize an inbound bridge event.
- **The request cannot be swapped between the alert and the reply.** `create_request` refuses while one is pending (`request_already_pending`) or while a grant exists (`grant_already_recorded`), and `cancel_request` is not exposed as a tool — it is only reached internally when the alert fails to send. So the tool/target the operator sees in the alert is the one that gets granted, which is why omitting the request id from the alert is safe rather than a gap.
- **The tool cannot be reached autonomously** — interactive `user_message`, non-service, and the active channel must equal the configured `operator_alert_channel` with injection enabled for it.
- **Approval is exact.** `_APPROVE_REPLIES = {"approve"}` after whitespace/case normalization, so "yes", "ok", or "approve please" do not grant. Strict is right here.
- **The grant is inert.** `consume_grant` exists and is deliberately unused — this leaf records consent and widens nothing, which is what #1198 will consume.
- **State is bounded** — 300s expiry, one-shot, and `clear_channel` drops everything when the in-flight turn ends.
- **Injection stays opt-in**, so existing deployments are unchanged.

Full suite locally: **8897 passed, 16 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Re-reviewed at `da09fc7a9`. The blocking gap is closed, and closed better than I asked.

I asked for the non-admin responder case. `test_resolved_nonoperator_responder_is_refused` is parametrized over `slack-U2` (`roles: [user]`) and a newly added `slack-U3` (`roles: [admin], is_service: true`) — an admin SERVICE identity, which is the harder case, since it satisfies `is_admin` and must still be refused.

That makes each half of the guard independently pinned. Re-running the mutation that survived, plus the two halves separately:

- drop both `is_admin` and `not is_service` → fails `[non-admin]` AND `[service-identity]`
- drop only `not is_service` → fails `[service-identity]`
- drop only `is_admin` → fails `[non-admin]`

So neither half can be removed silently by a later refactor. A single combined test would have let one half rot; this does not.

Everything from the prior review still holds — identity and ingress are server-owned, the request cannot be swapped between the alert and the reply, the tool is unreachable from autonomous triggers, approval is exact-match, the grant is inert until #1198 consumes it, and injection stays opt-in.

Full suite locally: **8899 passed, 16 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

Approved. Leaving it open per the operator; not merging.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Addressed the blocking gap in `da09fc7a9`.

Added a direct `record_authenticated_response` regression parametrized over:
- resolved non-admin responder (`slack-U2`)
- resolved admin-role service identity (`slack-U3`, `is_service: true`)

Both must return `unauthenticated_operator`, preserve the pending request, and record no grant. This directly pins both conjuncts in `_is_authenticated_operator`; deleting the admin/non-service guard now fails the test.

Local scoped validation was attempted through the bound runner, but it failed before pytest because the runner could not read its redacted `uv.toml` (`Permission denied`). The previous head had 9/9 green checks and Jason reported the full suite at 8897 passed; fresh CI is now running on the pushed test-only commit.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1204: saga: autonomous turns can recall 4% of the agent's own memory — the full-corpus read flag was never set on the pollers or heartbeat

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `98716fe91`. This is the shape I hoped for: the flag is granted per principal with reasons recorded, the blanket path is closed, and the widening is proven to be read-only.

## The guards hold under mutation

- flip the builder default to `True` → fails `test_trusted_service_without_corpus_declaration_is_narrow` for BOTH `poller:new-feed` and `scheduler:new-job`, plus `test_full_corpus_flag_changes_only_saga_read_authority`. The blanket-default failure mode is pinned.
- weaken the manifest parse to `bool(raw.get(...))` → fails `test_poller_full_corpus_read_requires_explicit_boolean_configuration`, so a truthy string like `"true"` cannot smuggle the grant in.

`test_full_corpus_flag_changes_only_saga_read_authority` asserting `replace(broad, saga_full_corpus_read=False) == narrow` is the cleanest possible statement of "read only, nothing else" — it makes the claim structurally rather than by enumerating fields that could drift.

## Against the leaf

- **Granted set is enumerable and asserted.** `test_full_corpus_read_grants_are_enumerated_across_static_and_builtin_principals` and `test_shipped_full_corpus_poller_grants_are_explicit_and_enumerated` mean a later principal cannot join silently — adding one fails a test.
- **Per-principal opt-in, not by-being-a-poller.** Heartbeat through its built-in profile, each shipped poller through its own manifest, builder default unchanged at `False`.
- **The authority decision is stated**, with a reason per principal, and the `legacy_admin` migration alternative is explicitly declined rather than ignored.
- **Re-measured and reported** — 2,083 / 2,083 per affected principal, produced the same way as the original 4.1% figure.
- **Tenant isolation survives** — `test_full_corpus_heartbeat_still_fails_closed_for_cross_tenant_output`.
- **Manifest key is additive and optional**, so manifests written before it still register.

Full suite locally: **8888 passed, 16 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

## Interaction worth recording — not blocking

The grant now covers the two ingest-heavy pollers, `gmail-inbox` and the two `social-cli` principals. Those turns are routinely tainted by attacker-influenceable content (an email body, a feed item), and `social-cli` holds a declared `run-social-cli.sh --platform --action ...` shell command, which can reach a public destination. So after this, a tainted social-cli turn can recall all 2,083 atoms and, in principle, wants a public sink.

It is safe today, and the reason is worth being explicit about: `ifc_label_blocked:shell_process` is precisely what stops it, and that is the single largest refusal class on these deployments. The corpus widening is therefore sound BECAUSE the taint gate holds on shell and public egress.

Two open leaves are about relaxing that boundary, and both preserve this:

- #1198 scopes any operator grant to a sink category and explicitly excludes `NETWORK`, `HTTP_WEBHOOK`, and `EXTERNAL_MCP`, and forbids autonomous triggers from requesting or holding one — so a poller cannot use it.
- #1196 gives autonomous turns the operator channel unconditionally, but that destination is the operator, not an attacker-reachable one.

Recording it so whoever builds #1198 or #1203 knows the corpus these principals can read is now the whole of it. If autonomous triggers ever gain a category grant covering `shell_process`, this composition becomes an exfiltration path and should be re-reviewed together.

Approved. Leaving it open per the operator; not merging.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1202: worklink: a superseded PR checkout lease blocks the next checkout for the rest of its 2-hour TTL, though it can no longer authorize anything

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `852ca6f56`. The release condition is derived the right way and every fail-closed path is pinned.

## What it does

On a lease conflict, `_observe_current_pr_head(scope)` reads the head from the configured forge adapter and validates it hard — number matches, state is `open`, `head_ref` matches the scope, and the SHA is 40 hex characters — raising on anything ambiguous. A lease whose recorded head differs from that observation is released; one that matches still produces the existing scope-conflict refusal.

Mutations on this head, each failing the tests that name the property:

- fail-open on observation failure → fails all three params of `test_acquire_keeps_foreign_lease_when_live_head_cannot_be_observed` (`network failure`, `unknown pull request`, `ambiguous response`)
- release even when work is retained → fails `test_acquire_refuses_to_release_superseded_lease_with_uncommitted_work`
- release a lease whose head still matches → fails `test_acquire_refuses_and_reports_foreign_scope_candidate`, `test_acquire_refuses_second_live_scope_for_same_target`, and `test_acquire_does_not_trust_new_scope_sha_to_release_matching_live_head`

That last one is the property I cared most about: release is driven by the SERVER observing the live head, and a caller-supplied scope SHA cannot cause a release. The test names it directly.

## Confirmed against the leaf

- **Retained work is not destroyed.** Before releasing, each stale lease is checked with `rev-parse HEAD` and `status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`; if HEAD moved from the recorded head or anything is dirty, the release is refused with a named error listing the candidates, and `pr_checkout_lease_retained` is emitted.
- **Release is auditable.** `pr_checkout_lease_superseded` carries `scope_id`, `superseded_head`, `observed_head`, and path.
- **One-scope-per-target survives.** A live second scope still refuses rather than being taken over.
- **The TTL backstop is untouched** — this adds an earlier release path rather than replacing expiry.

Full suite locally: **8889 passed, 16 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

## Note — not blocking

`_observe_current_pr_head` makes a network call while `fcntl.flock(directory_fd, LOCK_EX)` is held (acquired at `:772`, released at `:915`, call at `:820`). It is bounded — the GitHub client uses `timeout: float = 20.0` — and it only runs when a foreign lease is present, so worst case is a 20-second hold in the conflict path against the 2-hour wait this removes. Good trade. Worth remembering if the lease path ever becomes hot, or if a forge adapter is added whose client does not carry a default timeout.

Approved. Leaving it open per the operator; not merging.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: ACP: integrate the Agent Client Protocol agent surface (closes #1073)

payload.author: mimir-carreira

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: Worklink #1201: worklink: the scoped test command dies before collection on an EACCES it does not name — two reviews degraded, one validated push withheld

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `244c1defe`. The root cause is found, proven, and fixed without widening anything — this is the hard half of the leaf done well. Two items.

## The root cause is right, and I confirmed the expensive half is necessary

`/var/lib/mimir-worklink/repo-test-checkouts/<scope>/<issue-attempt>` at mode `0700` uid 1001 gid 1002, with the worker at euid/egid 1002 and no supplementary groups. That is outside `/workspace`, which is why my own search for the file found nothing.

I tested whether `UV_NO_CONFIG=1` alone would suffice, since the `copytree` is ~572 MB per run and `repo_test` ran 182 times in the measured window. It does not: entering a checkout by fd with an unsearchable parent fails identically with and without it, because uv canonicalizes the physical cwd before any config decision (`Current directory does not exist`). So the second disposable copy is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces, and the cost is justified.

The fix widens no mode and does not change worker identity, which was the criterion I most wanted held.

## Blocking — the diagnostic reports assumed identity as measured identity

```python
_WORKLINK_UID = 1002
_WORKLINK_GID = 1002
...
"runner_effective_uid": _WORKLINK_UID,
"runner_effective_gid": _WORKLINK_GID,
```

These are emitted as the runner effective ids but are compile-time constants. `_worker_can_search()` also decides which permission bits matter from them, so on a deployment numbered differently the walk picks the wrong bit, may name the wrong closest-failed ancestor or none, and prints confidently wrong uid/gid. For a leaf whose entire purpose is making this failure diagnosable, a diagnostic that can lie is worse than one that is absent.

This is #1439 exactly, and it adds a THIRD independent hardcoding site after `worklink/checkout.py:22-23` and `worklink/worker_exec.py:28-30`.

`project_tests.py` already imports from `.worklink.backends.registry`, so importing the existing constants rather than redeclaring them is available today and would let #1439 fix all sites at once. Better still: have the worker report its real `os.geteuid()`/`os.getegid()` in the launch response, since the worker is the process that actually knows. Either is small; the redeclaration is what I am asking to remove.

## Should fix — the regression pins a third-party tool version

`test_uv_config_search_is_bounded_at_unsearchable_snapshot_boundary` asserts `returncode == 2`. That is uv 0.12.3 specific. On uv 0.9.26 the same condition exits 1 with `Current directory does not exist`, so the test fails for any developer whose uv differs, and will break on a uv bump even though our behaviour is unchanged. CI is green only because the runner pins 0.12.3.

Assert the invariant we own — non-zero exit plus the `test_path_permission_denied` refusal and the diagnostic fields our code emits — rather than uv exit code 2 and its wording.

## Confirmed

- Removing `runner_effective_uid`/`gid` fails `test_project_test_permission_refusal_names_path_metadata_and_identity` by name, so the fields are pinned.
- `redact_text` is applied to both `path` and `traversal_failed`, and no file content is read or emitted.
- Both disposable copies are removed after the run.
- CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Re-reviewed at `747ad5182`. Both items are resolved.

**Constants** — `_WORKLINK_UID`/`_WORKLINK_GID` are gone; `project_tests.py` and the test now import `WORKLINK_UID`/`WORKLINK_GID` from `worklink.worker_exec`. That is the option I said would satisfy the ask, and it leaves #1439 able to fix every site from one definition instead of three.

**The uv assertion** — replaced correctly, and the new shape is better than what I asked for. `assert observed.returncode != 0` is now a PRECONDITION establishing that the boundary genuinely breaks the launch, and the real assertion is `assert result.ok is True` after the execution copy. So the test pins our invariant (the fix works) instead of uv exit code 2 and its exact wording, and it no longer breaks on a uv bump.

Mutations on this head:

- disable the execution copy (`_execution_checkout_fd` returns `os.dup` unconditionally) → fails `test_uv_config_search_is_bounded_at_unsearchable_snapshot_boundary`
- drop `runner_effective_uid`/`gid` from the diagnostic → fails `test_project_test_permission_refusal_names_path_metadata_and_identity`

Both guards are pinned.

CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

## One local failure, and it is not this PR

My local full suite is **1 failed, 8883 passed, 16 skipped**, and the failure is `test_uv_config_search_is_bounded_at_unsearchable_snapshot_boundary`:

```
ProjectTestRefusal: project test command or environment contains a controller path
```

My `uv` lives at `/Users/jcarreira/.local/bin/uv`, under the home directory, which the scrubber flags as a controller path — the test never reaches the assertion. That is my machine layout, not a defect here, and CI is green.

Recording it because it is adjacent to #1194 (the suite passing cross-platform). Two things a future pass might want, neither blocking and neither in scope for this leaf:

- the test could resolve `uv` from a location the scrubber admits, so a developer whose toolchain sits under `$HOME` is not permanently red on this test;
- `_execution_checkout_fd` copies from `/proc/self/fd/<n>`, which does not exist on macOS, so this path is Linux-only by construction. That is correct for the containment worker, which only runs in the container — worth knowing rather than fixing.

Approved. Leaving it open per the operator; not merging.

- Relaxed the uv regression to assert only the owned invariant (`returncode != 0`) before exercising the contained-copy success path; it no longer pins uv 0.12.3's exit code or error wording.

payload.title: Worklink #1200: worklink: the scoped checkout hands the runner files it cannot use — hardlinked executables lose +x, and a redacted file was unreadable enough to withhold a validated push

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Verified at `d6a96c395`. Defect A is fixed, the guards are pinned, and the change also closes a latent world-permission leak the PR does not claim.

Measured against `_normalize_directory_fd` before and after, across modes and link counts:

| in | nlink | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0o700` | 1 | `0o760` | `0o770` |
| `0o700` | 2 | `0o660` (lost +x) | `0o770` |
| `0o755` | 1 | **`0o771` — world-executable** | `0o770` |
| `0o755` | 2 | `0o660` (lost +x) | `0o770` |
| `0o644` | 1 or 2 | `0o660` | `0o660` |

The `0o755`/nlink-1 row is worth calling out: the previous `value.st_mode & 0o111` derivation produced `0o660 | 0o111 = 0o771`, so any ordinary committed script became world-executable after normalization. The old assertion used `0o700`, which is precisely why neither that nor Defect A was caught. Deriving a fixed `0o110` fixes both at once.

Mutations on this head, all caught by `test_fd_normalization_breaks_hardlinks_and_sets_shared_modes` in BOTH `[single-link]` and `[hardlinked]` parameters:

- restore the post-copy derivation (the original defect) → both fail
- `execute_bits = 0o110` unconditionally → both fail, so the non-executable case is pinned
- `execute_bits = 0o111` → both fail, so the world bit is pinned

Full suite locally: **8882 passed, 16 skipped**. CI 9/9 including `pytest-enforced`.

On Defect B: the PR does exactly what the leaf asked -- reports it could not be reproduced in the sandbox, declines to claim Defect A caused it, and names the evidence that would settle it. That is the right call and I am not treating it as unfinished work here.

For the record, since it moves B along: there is no `uv.toml` anywhere in the deployment -- no file, no `UV_*` environment, no uv config. `uv` searches upward for config, and an unreadable directory in that walk returns `EACCES` rather than `ENOENT`, which is what surfaces as "cannot read uv.toml". The `0o700`/`0o710` ancestor chmods at `checkout.py:470-473` are not the cause; the live lease and worklink directories are all `drwxr-xr-x 1001 1001`. B is being carried to its own leaf with a fresh recurrence from 2026-08-14T00:27.

Approved.
